# dtcloud_network (Data Source)

Looks up one network by id.

Use it to reference a network Terraform did not create, which is the common case, since networks
tend to outlive the things attached to them. Declaring one as a resource instead would hand Terraform
ownership of it, and a later `terraform destroy` would take it down with everything else.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "dtcloud_network" "app" {
  id = var.network_id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `id` (String) ID of the network to look up.

### Read-Only

- `allocation_pools` (List of Object) Address ranges the subnet allocates from. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--allocation_pools))
- `cidr` (String) Address range of the subnet.
- `dns_nameservers` (List of String) DNS servers advertised on this network.
- `enable_dhcp` (Boolean) Whether the subnet hands out addresses over DHCP.
- `gateway_ip` (String) Gateway address of the subnet.
- `ip_version` (Number) IP version of the subnet.
- `ipam_enabled` (Boolean) Whether the platform manages addressing, i.e. whether there is a subnet.
- `name` (String) Name of the network.
- `network_type` (String) Virtual or Physical.
- `subnet_id` (String) ID of the subnet, empty when IPAM is off.

<a id="nestedatt--allocation_pools"></a>
### Nested Schema for `allocation_pools`

Read-Only:

- `end` (String)
- `start` (String)

## Behaviour worth knowing

~> **A network with IPAM off has no subnet**, so `subnet_id`, `cidr`, `gateway_ip`, `enable_dhcp`,
`ip_version`, `dns_nameservers` and `allocation_pools` are empty. Check `ipam_enabled` before relying
on them.

* **A network that does not exist is an error**, not an empty result.
